name: Spence Job Market Signaling Model
description: Michael Spence's (1973) job market signaling model showing how education serves as a signal of worker productivity even without increasing it. Demonstrates separating equilibrium where high-ability workers signal through costly education. Spence received the 2001 Nobel Prize.

flows.name: HA Education
flows.equation: IF Wage_Premium > High_Ability_Education_Cost THEN High_Ability_Uneducated * Education_Rate ELSE 0

flows.name: LA Education
flows.equation: IF Wage_Premium > Low_Ability_Education_Cost THEN Low_Ability_Uneducated * Education_Rate ELSE 0

variables.name: Educated Expected Productivity
variables.equation: IF Total_Educated > 0 THEN (High_Ability_Educated * High_Productivity + Low_Ability_Educated * Low_Productivity) / Total_Educated ELSE High_Productivity

variables.name: Uneducated Expected Productivity
variables.equation: IF Total_Uneducated > 0 THEN (High_Ability_Uneducated * High_Productivity + Low_Ability_Uneducated * Low_Productivity) / Total_Uneducated ELSE Low_Productivity

reference: Spence M. Job Market Signaling. Quarterly Journal of Economics. 1973;87(3):355-374.
